Monir Ahmed, Principal, T & T College, Motijheel, Dhaka ------Petitioner
Vs.
Chairman, Governing Body, T & T College, Motijheel, Dhaka & others ------Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed, J: This Rule calls in question the propriety of the order dated 28.1.1998 passed by the District Judge, Dhaka in Misc. Appeal 28 of 1998 not granting ad interim injunction restraining the opposite parties to give effect to the decision taken in the Meeting dated 22.11.1997 of the governing body of the T & T College, Dhaka, inter alia, suspending the plaintiff petitioner from the post and position of the Principal of the said college. 

 2. Plaintiff was working as the Principal of the T & T College, Dhaka as averred since 1974. It is a private, but government affiliated Degree College having a large number of students imparting education to them. 

 3. The plaintiff Manir Ahmed has filed Title Suit 10 of 1998 of 131 of 1998, before the 4th Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka for declaration that the resolutions taken in the meeting of the governing body of the college on 22.11.1997 are illegal, without jurisdiction, collusive and violative of the service rules of the National University and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 In that meeting the resolutions were taken which are impugned in the suit to the effect that the plaintiff who was the principal of the college, was suspended temporarily from his post. Defendant 3 Saydur Rahman. Vice-principal was authorised and empowered to act as the principal of the college. A five Members enquiry committee was constituted to investigate the allegations brought against the plaintiff Principal. The defendant 3 was authorised and directed to take charge as acting Principal from the plaintiff and to work as the Principal. 

 5. The allegations brought against the plaintiff inter alia are continuous in subordination, professional misconduct, misappropriation of money from college fund, maladministration and corruption etc. On the same date by filing the suit an application under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure was tiled with prayer for temporary and ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants 1 to 3 from entering into the college premises, dispossessing the plaintiff from his office and interfering with the clay to clay works of the plaintiff in the college and also it was prayed that the defendants 4-7 should be restrained from working as members of the enquiry committee. 

 6. Defendant 3, the acting Principal already appeared on the date of filing the suit before the Assistant Judge and prayed for some time to file written objection against the prayer for temporary and ad-interim injunction of the plaintiff. 

 8. Against the said order dated 13.1.1998, the plaintiff preferred Misc. Appeal 20 of 1998 before the District Judge, Dhaka on 18.1.1998. In the said Misc. Appeal, an application was filed under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure for temporary and ad-interim injunction to the aforesaid effect, i.e. to stay the operation of the resolution of the said meeting. In the Court of the District Judge, the defendant No. 3 again appeared on the date of filing the appeal and prayed for some time to file written objection against the prayer for temporary and ad-interim injunction. The District Judge asked the defendants respondent to file written objection against the prayer of the appellant within seven days and refused to grant ad-interim injunction by his order dated 18.1.1998. 

 9. The present Rule has been obtained by the plaintiff appellant against that order. The Rule was issued on 28.1.1998. On the date of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the decision taken in the said meeting dated 22.11.1997 was stayed pending hearing of the Rule. 

 10. The defendant 3, the acting Principal and other defendant-opposite parties who were Members present in the said meeting, who have been made defendants in the suit, appeared by filing power in this court and filed counter affidavit. Plaintiff also filed reply of the same. Both the parties in fact, submitted their necessary papers and documents which are voluminous because they could not contest in the lower courts and file their papers. 

 12. The suit is pending before the Assistant Judge and the appeal is pending before the District judge. The defendants have not yet filed any written statement in the Court of trial or in the Court of appeal. Very horridly the plaintiff has come up before this court under the aforesaid circumstances. 

 13. Plaintiff claims that he is still in the office of the college and is working as the Principal and is running the college. 

 14. The claim of the opposite party No. 3 who is the defendant No. 3 the former Vice-Principal now acting Principal claims that he has taken over charge in compliance of the resolutions of the said meeting, has assumed the office and is running the college and is in seisin of the office as the Principal. He also claims that the plaintiff Principal is not in the office any more. 

 15. It is claimed by the defendants opposite parties that the plaintiff is absent from the college since 3.12.1997. The claim of the defendant No. 3 is supported by a letter/memorandum dated 14.2.1988 submitted by 187 students both male and female of different classes to the Chairman of the college governing body stating therein that the present acting Principal is running the college. It's administration works, examination of the students as per schedule, according to the decision of the said meeting dated 22.11.1997 effectively and the suspended Principal is absent from the college since 3.12.1997 (The memorandum of the students is on record and has been filed by the opposite party No. 3). 

 18. The case of the plaintiff is that the suspension order is apparently illegal and without jurisdiction as no prior notice was served upon him giving opportunity to explain the allegations brought against him. 

 21. It is noticed that the meeting was convened by the Chairman of the governing body of the college in accordance with Rule 18 as referred above. Necessary 5 Members of the governing body making corm were present in the meeting. It is not denied that the former Principal was not given prior opportunity to explain the allegations brought against him and this is the most important contention of the plaintiff in this litigation. 

 22. Arguments advanced on behalf of the defendant's side inter alia are that the question of suspension order is not a punishment. It is a stop gap arrangement for fair and legal investigation of the allegations brought against the plaintiff, to the held by the enquiry committee which has been constituted as per Rule 16(ka). It is also argued that the former Principal who was the Member-Secretary of the governing body of the college but he did not convene any meeting for long time despite repeated requests made by the Chairman vide letters dated 27.2.97 and 1.1.3.97 etc. and also demand made by the governing body repeatedly and hence the said meeting was convened by the Chairman legally as an Emergency (Talabi) Meeting on the allegations plaintiff were pending against the plaintiff Principal for a long time for necessary investigation. 

 24. The suit is pending to decide the question of legality of the suspension order of the plaintiff and other resolutions of the said meeting, which can only be decided on adducing evidence by both the parties in the trial court. 

 26. It is the settled principle of law that to got an order of temporary injunction or ad-interim injunction, the plaintiff must prove a prima facie case and also it must be shown that the balance of convenience and inconvenience of granting injunction is in favour of the plaintiff. 

 27. It is clear that the present plaintiff without giving necessary time and opportunity to the defendant to show cause against the prayer of temporary injunction, either in the trial court or in the appellate court, has rushed to this court in revision which is earmarked to see whether failure of justice is there in the impugned order. 

 "In order to obtain an order of temporary injunction, petitioners must establish that they have a good prima facie case and they will suffer irreparable injury if no such injunction is granted in their favour." 

 It is also very important whether the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the former Principal who is the plaintiff or it is in favour of the defendant No. 3. Many important activities, as referred above, concerning the education of large number of student have been completed by the present acting Principal by this time which cannot be destroyed or upset. In that case. It will create havoc in the life of many students and also some mischief may occur concerning the students their education and the college itself as in the petition for temporary injunction terms like দখল/বেদখল which means possession and dispossession has been used. It is very unfortunate that two higher educated persons are fighting like two war lords as if in enemy war concerning the educational institution which involves large number of students alleging their possession and dispossession like that of char land, as it is submitted that about one dozen of cases both civil and criminal are pending between the parties. 

 "Temporary injunction likely to cause mischief cannot be granted: when it is clear that grant of temporary injunction which the plaintiff sought will really tell up the internal management of the college itself the plaintiff is not entitled to such a relief." 

 It is held that in the present case, the plaintiff has been put under suspension temporarily which is not a punishment, now the enquiry will be held by the enquiry committee which has been constituted. It shall not be stopped for legal and correct investigation. 

 First, the plaintiff has to establish a prima facie case, secondly, it was to be shown that the plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss if the injunction prayed for is not granted and thirdly, the balance of convenience lies in favour of the plaintiff and in favour of the granting the temporary injunction prayed for." 

 The plaintiff, former Principal shall not irreparable loss in any manner during the pendency of the suit in which he validity of the suspension order shall be decided on merits after hearing the parties on adducing evidence, on the other hand, if the injunction is granted here will be chaos and confusion, as to the running of administration of the allege itself, the students will face caastrophe in respect of their studies and examination etc. The enquiry of the allegation against the delinquent may not be fair. At the same time the institution where there are more than 12.000 students as submitted by the parties getting their education in a poor country like ours shall not be allowed to be laid down before two fighting groups which have already been created as is understood. 

 Plaintiff can have temporary in-junction in a suit if he succeeds to make out a good prima facie case and the good prima facie case has been explained to mean that a serious question is to he tried in the suit and that in the event of 'success, if the injunction be not granted, the plaintiff would suffer irreparable injury. 

 In all the decisions referred above, their Lordships were of the common and same view that when the plaintiff has no prima facie case, balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the defendant and is against the plaintiff, if injunction is not granted, the plaintiff will not incur irreparable loss if temporary injunction creates any mischief to the subject matter injunction should not be granted.
